highlights.title: Trump commercial railing against his enemies kept airing after court blocked it
highlights.summary: Trump commercials paid for by the US government continued airing on TV the day after a judge blocked the ads because they likely violate a US law against government-funded publicity or propaganda.
body: In the most widely aired commercial, Trump railed against his perceived enemies and said he would “liberate America from these villains once and for all.” The campaign also included a commercial praising Trump’s record as president, another in which Trump calls the US the “most exceptional nation ever to exist in human history,” and commercials related to the Iran war and the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

US District Judge Jennifer Rochon issued a temporary restraining order (TRO) blocking the ads on Sunday, October 11, which took effect at 6:45 pm that night. The order said the government must cancel the ads, “including those placements for the evening of October 11, 2026.”

The Trump administration had told the court on October 10 that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) advertising purchases were set to expire on October 11 and would not be renewed. Despite that, the ads continued airing the night of October 11 and on part of October 12. This was also a week after Trump’s October 5 statement that he would start paying for the ads “myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”

The employee, 35-year-old Abdulrahman Alfozan, is charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, according to a report from The…
body: The recording device was apparently discovered plugged into a TV’s USB port in an executive meeting room.
OpenAI’s post about the incident says it used its AI models to “understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier.”

As reported by The San Francisco Standard, OpenAI found the device plugged into a TV’s USB port in an executive conference room. The device was reportedly covered in toilet paper and installed on or around September 28th.

OpenAI says it fired the employee and referred the incident to the FBI. According to the Standard, he was arrested Friday and has remained in custody since, appearing in federal court for the first time on Tuesday.

highlights.title: McIlroy: LIV Golf was half a good idea
highlights.summary: Rory McIlroy believes LIV Golf was "half a good idea, executed poorly" and the breakaway is no longer a threat to the traditional game as it tries to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy.
body: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) ploughed in £3.7bn over four years, luring the likes of Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau away from the PGA Tour, before withdrawing its support this year.

That led to Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States with a view to relaunching as LIV 2.0, having received a potential $300m (£227m) backing from BC Partners Capital providing a specified number of players re-sign for the new venture.

Rahm has already announced he will not be continuing and news this week that any player signing up for LIV will be barred from DP World Tour membership and Ryder Cup eligibility has delivered a crippling blow.

"LIV had probably like, half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly," McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy forum in New Delhi, where he is playing this week in the DP World India Championship.

highlights.title: 63 Years Later, the Best 'Peanuts' Sally Line Is Still an Iconic Comic Strip Quote
highlights.summary: In almost 50 years, however, despite taking more Ls than a stuck typewriter, Charlie Brown almost never actually got mad about it. His style is more of a world-weary acceptance, verging on Zen calm. It's left to other characters to rage, cry, and question their lot.
body: Charlie Brown is one of the most consistently unlucky characters in Western fiction. The degree to which life and the universe conspire to dump misfortune directly on his head is the beating heart of Charles Schulz's Peanuts. If you've got any problems at all, you can see what Charlie Brown's up to and be slightly cheered up by the knowledge that at least you've got it better than him.

When modern fans talk about Peanuts, all of Sally's best-remembered moments usually have to do with either her constant innocent windmill dunks on Charlie Brown or her deeply one-sided crush on Linus. On a reread, however, what really stood out about Sally is her antagonistic relationship with academia.

Sally is Peanuts' patron saint of unwilling students. Most of the rest of the Peanuts gang never seemed to mind their studies. ( Patty isn't good at school, but she didn't actively resent it the way that Sally does.) If you were one of those kids who did their level best to try to wriggle out from under the burden of public schooling, Sally was your representation in the Peanuts crew.

highlights.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
highlights.summary: AI leaders joined whistleblowers and security leaders at a sweeping parliamentary session, while a few hundred meters away Britain’s spy chief warned AI could be used to create new bioweapons.
body: Representatives for OpenAI and Anthropic told a British parliamentary hearing that voluntary pledges were no longer enough to ensure safety and that new laws should be introduced, deepening a public schism with Google DeepMind and Meta, both of which declined to back new legislation.

The Business, Innovation, Science, and Trade Committee, comprising a cross-party panel of MPs, held an evidence session on Tuesday with appearances from four frontier AI firms, four former staff of the firms turned whistleblowers and senior British civil servants.

“The rules should be binding,” Anthropic’s head of Europe Liam Booth-Smith told the committee, when asked if the company’s view was that AI safety now needs a statutory framework. The company, he said, has “consistently believed that there should be binding rules on companies and that voluntary commitments are not enough.”

highlights.title: MIT Lincoln Laboratory hosts National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology
highlights.summary: MIT Lincoln Laboratory hosted the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology (NSCEB) for a stop on its national roadshow. The event convened representatives of state organizations, defense centers, universities, technology companies, and business executives to discuss how Massachusetts'…
body: "We have a lot to leverage in this region to advance biotechnology," said Christina Rudzinski, assistant head of the Biotechnology and Human Systems Division at Lincoln Laboratory. "Many people are already working together to push the bioindustrial sector beyond biopharmaceuticals and into a broader ecosystem across industries. This synergy is where NSCEB comes in — connecting policy to the real-world work already happening, including here at Lincoln Laboratory and across the state."

Biotechnology touches many economic and defense sectors, from disease-resistant crops and lifesaving medicines to biofuels and advanced manufacturing materials. In 2022, Congress established the NSCEB to study the national security implications of this rapidly advancing field and issue policy recommendations to ensure continued U.S. leadership.

In April 2025, the 11-member bipartisan and bicameral commission released its report, calling for a minimum of $15 billion in federal investment over five years. According to the report, China is investing aggressively to dominate the field, echoing a pattern the United States has seen before in sectors such as semiconductors.

highlights.title: 'State of the Game' report finds most English clubs living on financial brink
highlights.summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster.
body: The IFR added that interest and investment from around the world continues to grow within English football, but the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform.

Despite over £9bn generated in revenue, 94 per cent of clubs are loss-making, with long-term security being put at risk through excessive short-term spending to keep up with rivals. This, the IFR says, has led to a "dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".
The report acknowledges that the success of the Premier League has driven economic success, making English football the "richest, best and most deeply competitive in the world".

However, it points to "financial cliff-edges between and within leagues", with the average Premier League club making more than eight times the revenues of an average Championship club, and the system of parachute payments paid by the Premier League to Championship clubs relegated contributing to significant overspend by clubs in the Championship.

highlights.title: K/DA Reactivates Social Accounts, Fueling Rumors of the Virtual K-pop Group’s Comeback After 6 Years
highlights.summary: Official K/DA accounts have been updated for the first time in six years. New profile and banner images continue to show the existing promotional art from the All Out era, now with the addition of hot pink flames.
body: K/DA, which debuted at the 2018 League of Legends World Championship, consists of four League champions (Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai'Sa) voiced by international pop-stars. The group’s first single, aptly called POP/STARS, was the first K-pop song by a girl group to receive RIAA Platinum certification in 2022. The early success of the girl group prompted the release of a full EP, All Out, in 2020.
Since then, the group has pretty much gone dark. K/DA skins still exist in-game, but there’s been no word on new music or performances. Until now.

An updated banner image continues to use promotional images from the All Out era, showing the main K/DA quartet alongside the era’s guest artist, Seraphine, who was a newly released champion at the time. As of October 13, however, those images also show the addition of hot pink and magenta flames.

Data-mined leaks from earlier this year already raised hopes that the group would have some role in the current season of League of Legends. Details in a Wild Rift update, first spotted by SkinSpotlights, pointed to a potential “Firestarter” skin concept, as well as a new song registered on the ASCAP Repertory.

highlights.title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
highlights.summary: Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience.
body: Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with decompiling and recompiling games.

Microsoft is putting together a new Xbox Labs group to explore the rapid emergence of these mods, many of which use AI models to help modders remix games in ways we’ve rarely seen before. Xbox Labs will be a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.”

Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.”

highlights.title: Hideo Kojima Reviews The Resident Evil Movie
highlights.summary: Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review. Kojima, a true cinephile known for his public movie reviews, said he "wasn't particularly interested" in seeing the movie at first, but he did, and he sounded pretty impressed by what he saw.
body: "Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing. From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end," he said.

Kojima went on to observe what others did as well, which is how the Resident Evil movie is more of a film that provides the "experience of playing Resident Evil" as opposed to watching an adaptation of one of its stories.

"It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996," he said. "I was just like [main character] Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol."

This is the kind of response that Cregger said he wanted viewers to have. It's also what got Cregger in some hot water with hardcore fans who wanted to see a straight adaptation of one of the games instead of Cregger's own original story set inside the world of Resident Evil.

highlights.title: Make an old, lumpy bed feel new again. Five mattress toppers that actually work
highlights.summary: A topper can make a good mattress great, or change the feel of a mattress to your comfort level. After many nights of testing, we’ve found the best of the best. The best sleep masks and best Bluetooth sleep masks in the US.
body: I f you make your bed, you’ve gotta lie in it, but a mattress topper can help make it a more pleasant experience. These pads sit on top of the mattress, adding an extra layer that can fundamentally change the feel, making it firmer, softer or just helping to smooth out bumps and lumps. None of these products can fix an old and broken mattress: if the springs are shot or there is a dip in the mattress the shape of a long-dead relative, you may need a new mattress. But if you are stuck with a mattress that is too hard or too soft, adding a mattress topper can make it juuusssst right.

I’ve had nearly sixty years of experience in sleeping, and for over half of that, I’ve been testing consumer products ranging from automatic coffee makers to xBox peripherals for publications including PC World, Reviewed.com, CNET and many others. For all of those publications, I bring an objective scientific eye to testing products and helping consumers make better buying decisions.
After this review was completed, I donated all of the mattress toppers to furniture banks in Massachusetts that provide household goods to families in need.

highlights.title: Google finally releases Gemini 4 Argon
highlights.summary: After months sitting on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, Google has finally launched its long-awaited Gemini 4 Argon model, claiming it can compete with the best the industry has to offer.
body: After months of trailing its rivals, Google says Argon competes with the industry’s best.

Google says Argon delivers “frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex workflows,” while cutting down on hedging, repetition, and the cliches that continue to plague AI chatbots. The company claims Argon outperforms rival models like GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5 across a range of benchmarks, including coding, cybersecurity, science, finance, and law.

Google says it’s already putting Argon to use internally, such as finding and patching cybersecurity vulnerabilities, halving the computing power needed to power YouTube’s comments section, and debugging the drone physics simulator for Alphabet’s drone delivery company Wing.

body: The move may be surprising. In September 2025, Disney joined others in publicly criticizing Character.AI for stealing content and harming kids. Specifically, Disney sent a strongly worded cease-and-desist letter that accused Character Technologies of weaponizing Disney characters “in a way that could damage its brand long term,” Axios reported.

“Character.AI’s infringing chatbots are known, in some cases, to be sexually exploitive and otherwise harmful and dangerous to children, offending Disney’s consumers and extraordinarily damaging Disney’s reputation and goodwill,” Disney wrote at the time.

That scandal ended with Character Technologies wiping all Disney-owned characters from its platform, but since then, Disney has hired former Character.AI chief Karandeep Anand as its first chief technology officer, Deadline reported.

Just to put it in perspective, you can currently get a semi-functional Pip-Boy replica from the IGN Store for only $300. Dark Horse also recently launched, in my opinion, a much cooler set of Fallout bookends for only $179.99.

highlights.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
highlights.summary: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.
body: Former gang boss Duane "Keffe D" Davis has been sentenced to at least 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.

A jury found Davis, 63, guilty in September of one count of murder with a deadly weapon for the rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on 7 September 1996. He has said he will appeal the verdict.

Prosecutors argued that although Davis did not fire the gun himself, he was the ringleader of the group that committed the murder. He admitted in his memoir that he had provided the gun used in the crime.
Davis' conviction was the first in a cold case that has intrigued hip-hop fans for nearly 30 years.

highlights.title: ‘You’re honoring a life well-lived’: embalmers describe their work (in great detail)
highlights.summary: Embalming is one of the most common options for temporarily preserving bodies after death – but what exactly does it entail? Most people don’t like to think about what happens to people’s bodies after they die. Victoria Bilstein is an exception.
body: “I’ve actually wanted to be an embalmer since I was 10 years old!” says the funeral director, embalmer and author based in the midwest. As a child, Bilstein had two leg surgeries that incorporated bones from two deceased donors. After that, she wondered about the people who had helped save her life and the families who had lost them.

She saw this work as an opportunity to help grieving families. “I wanted to be able to do postmortem reconstruction on donors so their families had the option for a viewing,” she says. “It felt like such an amazing way to honor my donors.” In her six years in the industry, she estimates she’s worked on at least a thousand embalmings.
Most people who are planning burials and viewings for loved ones choose to have them embalmed.

But fewer and fewer American families are choosing burials. According to the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA), the burial rate in 2025 was 31.6%, while the cremation rate was 63.4%. By 2045, the NFDA expects the cremation rate to reach 82.3%.

highlights.title: The Paris Auto Show is full of interesting cars Americans can’t have

The big trade shows for cars were a gateway drug for many, expos where you could see the newest models of today and the concepts of tomorrow. But automakers increasingly got tired of sharing the spotlight with each other.
body: But the news out of Paris, where its auto show held media day yesterday, seems like we stepped back into a time when automakers would debut new cars aplenty. That retro vibe extends to the cars themselves, with plenty of familiar nameplates reimagined.

France’s Renault has a long and glorious history of delightful concept cars, and more on what it brought to Paris later. But the star of the show was arguably Stellantis, with strong work from Citroen, Peugeot, and Fiat, to name but three. But this article is meant to irritate you, because I’m pretty sure none of the stuff you’re seeing here will come to the United States. And it’s doubly irritating considering what Stellantis’ brands do offer us over here, doubling down on the same malign trends I saw back in 2020: did you know they’re about to relaunch a V8 Hellcat-powered Charger?

highlights.title: Higgsfield takes AI video from 1 minute to over 10
highlights.summary: Higgsfield brings creators longer videos with GPT-6 Astra, precise visuals with GPT-Image-2.5, and a path to voice filmmaking with GPT-Live.
body: Higgsfield AI ⁠ (opens in a new window) is on a mission to make professional video and image creation accessible to anyone with an idea. Before GPT‑6 Astra, those videos topped out at around one minute. Now, says CEO and co-founder Alex Mashrabov, users can create videos over 10 minutes long.

Longer videos are just one way Higgsfield AI helps smaller creative teams take on more ambitious work. According to Alex, with models like GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑Image‑2.5, it’s now possible for a single creator to execute high-end fashion campaigns from start to finish.

Higgsfield AI’s creative agents take on repetitive production tasks, such as creating multiple variations of a shot. With GPT‑6 Astra, those agents can also call external tools to handle complex, manual work in 3D modeling. Alex says that capability helps address one of creative AI’s hardest problems: maintaining consistency across longer videos.
points: Higgsfield brings creators longer videos with GPT-6 Astra, precise visuals with GPT-Image-2.5, and a path to voice filmmaking with GPT-Live.

highlights.title: Xbox Announces Xbox Labs, Aimed in Part at Getting Improved Old-Gen Games Playable in Web Browsers
highlights.summary: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.
body: No doubt seeing the growing community of games getting improved versions ported into web browsers (like the 94fps browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved), Microsoft itself is keen to get in on the action in support of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's goal of reaching 1 billion players per day.

Xbox has been tinkering with running Xbox and Xbox 360 games in browsers, and the Xbox Labs initiative is a formalization of those efforts that will see a small team of engineers playing with emerging technologies in order to find new ways for games new and old to be distributed and even created. And IGN understands that this won't just be an R&D effort; rather, Xbox Labs is tasked with shipping products – Sharma says, "We'll build in the open" – and getting gamers to engage with them.
